record.one_liner: Managed cloud database platform for MongoDB, with an Atlas Administration API for managing clusters, projects and users.
record.auth_notes: Service account access tokens (OAuth 2.0 client credentials) are recommended. API keys use HTTP Digest auth and are the legacy method.
record.access_notes: Free-forever M0 tier exists, and the Clusters API can create Free clusters. Creating service accounts or API keys requires Organization Owner access, which the creator of a self-serve org has. critic: free access confirmed via the free-cluster limits page (Free cluster creatable through the API); no paid-plan gate found for the Admin API.
record.api_notes: Endpoints follow /api/atlas/<version>/groups/<GROUP-ID>/ paths. Breadth judged from the Admin API v2 reference (clusters, projects, users, etc.).

evidence.quote: To create a service account or API keys for an organization, you must have Organization Owner access to that organization.
You can create a Free cluster using the Clusters API resource.
Yes, MongoDB Atlas offers a free-forever tier, the M0.
Many Atlas Administration API endpoint URLs follow the format of /api/atlas/<version>/groups/<GROUP-ID>/
MongoDB Atlas Managed MCP Server, which MongoDB hosts and manages for you in Atlas.
Service accounts are the recommended method to manage authentication to the Atlas Administration API.

input.query: MongoDB Atlas Administration API free account create API key without paid plan M0 cluster
